title: Correlation: When Two Things Move Together

scenes.narration: Does studying more really raise your marks? Let's look at real data, and see what correlation tells us.
Each dot is one student. Hours studied go on the bottom. Marks go up the side. The line shows the trend, and it goes up.

props.title: Hours studied vs marks
props.formula:
r is close to +1
strong positive

scenes.narration: The correlation coefficient r runs from minus one to plus one. Close to plus one means both rise together. Close to zero means no clear link.
Careful. Correlation is not causation. Ice cream sales and drowning both rise in summer. Something else, the heat, drives both.
Quick recap. Correlation measures a link. It does not prove cause. Your practice task: plot two columns from your own data and look at the trend.

props.title: Recap
items: Always plot before you trust r
